edits.title: Reuse a URL-keyed evidence cache for table extraction
edits.content: For a bounded table-research task, keep fetched text in a URL-keyed dictionary. Deduplicate candidate URLs and exclude cached URLs before batching fetches; retain successful responses and exclude failed responses from extraction evidence. Supply cached URL/text pairs together to a schema-validated extraction call. Use the same cache to verify that every cited URL was fetched and every nonempty quotation occurs verbatim in its cited text. Check source hostnames with exact-domain or dot-delimited subdomain matching, then verify exact requested row coverage and cell keys before recording constraint checks. Cache reuse avoids another backend fetch. These checks establish intermediate evidence consistency; they do not by themselves establish successful final submission.

proposal.summary: Refine discovery identity handling and evidence-completeness checks. Existing fetch-recovery guidance remains supported.

edits.title: Inspect discoveries and reconcile name variants
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders can cause stalled_search signals even when later calls record entities. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, handle each query in input order. Compare identities rather than raw name strings: reconcile supported variants involving initials, shortened names, or apostrophe styles with existing entities before recording discoveries. Keep aliases as evidence metadata, not new entities; do not merge ambiguous names without supporting context. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including searches that successfully verify fields for known entities. Such searches can advance evidence coverage despite a stalled_search signal. Never invent discoveries to suppress a warning.

edits.title: Recover and validate incomplete rendered evidence
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific missing fields before fetching again. Request concise factual summaries with brief supporting excerpts instead of full-page reproduction. Test the revised focus on one page and inspect the evidence before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus. Keep unstated fields unresolved and use alternative sources rather than inferring facts from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. Validate quotations against an individual saved response, then separately review whether they support the correct entity, field, time, and required scope. A nonempty value and matching quotation do not establish completeness: track summaries, truncated excerpts, and unresolved attribution as outstanding gaps. For exact wording, retrieve the complete required statement; do not insert editorial gap notes into factual values. Preserve shared attribution when applying a statement to multiple entities. Give reviewers the actual contract, including whether quotations must match rendered responses or original page text, and each field's time scope. Repair concrete defects, rerun structural and quotation checks, and review the repaired fields before submission. FETCH_FAILED requires the separate bounded retry and source-switching procedure.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern follow-up research on already discovered entities: six year-level nationality queries, three targeted affiliation/nationality queries, four individual nationality queries, and three final audit queries. Their empty discovery records are consistent with verification rather than failed discovery; several supplied evidence used in the final output. Existing memory explicitly permits honest empty records for verification. Repeated signals across recorded outcomes therefore do not establish that this guidance is ineffective.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel-domain requests, two early alternative-source failures, three nationality-source failures, two later university/news failures, two biography/CV failures, and two final Nature failures. The run excluded attempted URLs, tested a small alternative-domain batch, reused saved hits, and recovered through other sources, including an alternate CV and a professional-society announcement. Existing memory covers this procedure and cautions against attributing failures to URL formatting. The outcomes show recovery rather than consistently harmful guidance; neither a permanent domain blacklist nor another retry rule is justified.

The discovery log counts omitted initials, added middle initials, apostrophe variants, and surnames alone as new entities after their full identities were already recorded. The trajectory's raw-string known_names comparison explains this inflation. Final rows avoided duplication, but the discovery bookkeeping failure remains reusable and belongs in the existing discovery memory.

Quotation checks repeatedly passed while a motivation remained truncated; later, even 'Missing cells: []' coexisted with an editorial note admitting incomplete evidence. Semantic audits identified this and attribution problems, and targeted retrieval repaired them before the successful final review. Earlier reviewers also questioned original-page quotation fidelity despite the rendered-text contract. Extend the existing recovery skill with separate completeness tracking and contract-aligned review rather than creating overlapping guidance. Its empty usage/outcome history provides no basis for deletion.
